summary: Georgia Tann ran the Memphis branch of the Tennessee Children's Home Society from the 1920s to 1950, abducting thousands of children from poor families to sell to wealthy adopters while hundreds died in her neglectful care.

evidence.note: born in Philadelphia, Mississippi in the 1890s to a local judge
settles in Memphis as executive director of the Tennessee Children's Home Society
eugenic objections to adoption (Goddard) that her blank-slate pitch overturned
juvenile judge Camille Kelly strips parental rights and hands children to Tann
Press-Scimitar Christmas baby ads market children like gifts
transport fees paid to her private box; markups up to thousands of dollars
social worker tricks widow Grace Gribble into signing away three children
overcrowded boarding homes, spoiled milk, denied medical treatment
estimated hundreds of infant deaths, including winter 1945 at the home
survivor accounts of sexual and physical abuse by Tann
cancer, Governor Browning's investigation announced weeks before her 1950 death
legacy of sealed adoption records still in force in many states

notes: Transcript spells the name Tan; standard spelling Tann used. Birth year 1891 from general knowledge (transcript garbled). main_span starts at her 1924 Memphis appointment (approximate); early placements in Mississippi and Texas are prelude. Opening segments on orphan trains and baby farms are background, so not in covered_span. Camille Kelly given floruit only; her dates are not in the packet.
